thread.title_full: Highland Springs soccer club program brings together multilingual learners, boosts school engagement

author: Old Dominion News
title: Highland Springs soccer club program brings together multilingual learners, boosts school engagement
text:
A soccer club at Highland Springs High School is helping multilingual learners feel more engaged at school, according to an April 22 report. The program was started by Assistant Principal JoAna Smith and brings together about a dozen students who practice soccer during the school day while speaking Spanish.
The initiative aims to support students who are learning English and help them connect with peers and staff. Smith said that focusing on relationships is important for student success. “Part of that is you have to be intentional with relationships with students and make connections with them,” she said. She added that the club has strengthened these connections.
Juan Mejia, a senior who serves as captain of the club, described how the program provides a welcome break from class. “It’s a different experience, because it’s in the middle of the school day, so it’s nice to have a moment out of class to enjoy what we like,” he said. Students participate twice weekly by stepping out of elective classes for half-hour practices.
Smith reported improvements in attendance, behavior, and grades among participants. She noted that academic requirements for the club are stricter than those set by the Virginia High School League because “I want to prepare them, not just to play but also to go on to college, where they have to maintain a GPA and attendance.” The idea for the club grew from an action-based research cohort Smith joined several years ago. Other Henrico schools have launched similar programs; Douglas S. Freeman High School’s principal John Marshall received an REB Award for his efforts in this area.
The Highland Springs program received funding from the Henrico Education Foundation for equipment and other needs. Josue Martinez, another participant speaking through a peer translator, said he enjoys practicing with others who speak his native language: “They’re giving opportunities to people who don’t get that many opportunities,” Josue said.
Henrico County Public Schools provide educational services throughout Henrico County near Richmond according to its official website . The district emphasizes positive learning experiences delivered by dedicated staff in both teaching and support roles as noted on its website . Educators within Henrico County Public Schools have earned REB Awards recognizing classroom performance and professional development per district information . Amy Cashwell serves as superintendent according to official sources , leading under the motto ‘The right to achieve. The support to succeed’ as stated by HCPS .
summary: The program was started by Assistant Principal JoAna Smith and brings together about a dozen students who practice soccer during the school day while speaking Spanish. Juan Mejia, a senior who serves as captain of the club, described how the program provides a welcome break from class.
